topics.topic: External disaster-recovery replay record: ownership, contents, survival, and failure handling
questions: What record is this, who creates and keeps it outside the lost store, what facts does it contain, and what happens when it is absent or incomplete?

What external record is this, who owns and protects it, what facts and ordering must it contain to replay erasures, restrictions and relationship ends, and how is its survival independent of the lost Registry store established?

quotes:
What the owner repeats after a restore — erasures, restrictions, ends of a
relationship — follows the owner's own record of the retention review
(R0-60).

This is the owner's operation (Explicit exclusions: the
   host's administration), and the owner's record is its evidence; Registry,
   which no longer holds those changes, cannot list them, enforce them or
   tell when this is done.
judgement.why: The custody, protection, completeness and loss handling of the owner's external operational record are disaster-recovery and governance notes outside Registry's State 0 product boundary.

topics.topic: Registry availability and observable recovery completion before privacy-state replay finishes
questions: May the restored Registry answer callers before lost erasures and restrictions have been repeated, thereby disclosing personal data that R0-06, R0-60, R0-65 and R0-67 say is gone or unavailable; and what observable event establishes that recovery is complete?
Can Registry serve callers after restoration but before these lost erasures and restrictions are reapplied, and what observable failure occurs if replay is incomplete or fails?

quotes:
The owner first starts the restored instance owner-only (A17 rule 1), so
   no service and no agent reaches it, and brings each Customer and project to
   the state the owner's own record of the retention review (R0-60) gives for
   it now — erased, restricted, ended or not — and erases audit entries before
   the latest date the owner erased by, before configuring the tokens and
   starting it again.

This is the owner's operation (Explicit exclusions: the
   host's administration), and the owner's record is its evidence; Registry,
   which no longer holds those changes, cannot list them, enforce them or
   tell when this is done. Its guarantee after a restore is what the backup
   held.
judgement.why: State 2 requires owner-only recovery with services and agents excluded until replay is finished, then token configuration and restart; it also expressly says Registry cannot itself signal completion.

topics.topic: Surviving repeat-import input after VPS retirement, including custody, fidelity, and failure handling
questions: After the VPS source has been retired and the one-time migration has ended, what named input remains available for the repeated import, and must it preserve the original selected projects, display names and aliases?
After the VPS source has been retired, what surviving input makes the import repeatable, who keeps it, and what happens if that input is unavailable or fails verification?

quotes:
A store lost before a checked backup holds the import
loses the import with it, and the import may then be made again.
The only source is the Registry on the VPS, imported once.

The local instance and the test rig are not sources; what they and the
VPS otherwise hold stays behind and is retired with its instance.

The owner makes the export of a source with a one-time migration script run on
that source's host. The script is not a Registry operation: production Registry
gains no export action, and the source keeps none after the migration.

The uploaded file is kept in the owner session that uploaded it, never in
   the store, until the import is accepted, another file is uploaded in that
   session, or the session ends (M11); then it is dropped.

The owner confirms that mapping in the confirmation
   step (A13 rule 6); the confirmation applies the file of that digest, the
   picks, names, aliases and Customer values the mapping showed, nothing
   else; a file no longer kept is refused and must be uploaded again.
judgement.divergence: One implementation or recovery procedure preserves the accepted export and its confirmed picks, names, aliases and Customer values outside the lost store, so the owner can reproduce the import; another discards them when the session ends and retires the VPS, so the owner either cannot repeat the import or reconstructs different imported data. The owner notices failure or a changed mapping, and consumers notice missing or differently named projects and links.
judgement.why: The promise that the lost import may be repeated depends on a surviving input and mapping that the texts expressly discard inside Registry but never assign to any external custodian.

topics.topic: Scope of post-backup changes that must be reconstructed during recovery
questions: Are these three actions exhaustive, or must the owner also reconstruct other post-backup changes such as lifted restrictions, resumed relationships, corrections, project erasures, grants, revocations and pointer changes?
